title: Locks, contention and deadlocks
brief: Design lock scope and ordering so waiting protects the intended decision.
outcomes: Choose a lockable authority with a sound isolation and snapshot protocol
Diagnose and bound contention and deadlocks
entry: Transaction snapshots and the class capacity rule.

heading.title: What a lock protects
heading.brief: Compare row, table and predicate protection, then use the existing session guard for capacity, including empty bookings; every capacity-changing writer must acquire that authority and hold it through commit. Develop a complete protocol with declared isolation: on PostgreSQL Read Committed, count in a separate fresh statement after acquiring the guard; contrast a conflicting guard update with whole-transaction retry and a Serializable protocol.

heading.title: Waiting and rechecking
heading.brief: Show on pinned PostgreSQL that a lock-only guard and a booking count on an already-established Repeatable Read snapshot can admit stale evidence after waiting. Verify the chosen repair with two native sessions; distinguish waiting, fresh statement visibility and a conflicting update/retry rather than claiming that acquiring a lock refreshes a snapshot.

heading.title: A cycle of waits
heading.brief: Give two sessions opposite product-lock order, draw their wait dependency and explain deadlock victim rollback and retry.

heading.title: Contention without a cycle
heading.brief: Bound transaction duration and waits, order acquisitions consistently and assess NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED only against their changed result contract.
